S1: Nvidia, the chip maker at the heart of the AI boom, has lost almost half its value in about seven weeks. On Friday alone, it fell fourteen percent. The Nasdaq had its worst week since March twenty twenty, and the S and P five hundred and the Dow slipped into a correction. So what happened? Is the AI bubble bursting? And what does it mean for the future of AI? Let's break it down.
S2: In early October, Nvidia closed at a record of about two hundred and thirty-nine dollars a share, worth close to six trillion dollars. By Friday's close, it was down to about one hundred and twenty-five dollars. That's a fall of around forty-seven percent. Last week alone, it dropped twenty-three percent, its worst week since October two thousand and eight.
S3: Reason one is money. Big tech companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on chips and data centres. Investors are now asking a simple question: how fast will all that spending turn into profit? Nvidia's latest results beat expectations, but the doubt didn't go away. When a stock is priced for perfection, doubt alone can push it down.
S4: Reason two is politics. After the US midterm elections on November third, investors began to worry about tighter rules for AI and more local opposition to new data centres. Reason three is leadership. On November twelfth, Nvidia's co-founder and chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned after thirty-three years. Finance chief Colette Kress is now interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent one.
S5: Reason four is interest rates. Markets now expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December. Higher rates make future profits worth less today. That hits fast-growing tech stocks hardest, because so much of their value depends on profits many years from now.
S6: Here's the maths of a crash. If you had put one thousand dollars into Nvidia at its October record, it would now be worth about five hundred and twenty-five dollars. To get back to one thousand, the stock now has to rise about ninety-one percent. In general, a fifty percent fall needs a one hundred percent gain just to break even.
S7: So, is the AI bubble bursting? Nobody knows for sure, but history offers two lessons. After the dot-com bubble in two thousand, the Nasdaq fell nearly eighty percent, yet the internet kept growing and changed the world. Nvidia itself fell about two-thirds in twenty twenty-two, before AI demand sent it to new records. Share prices and technology can move very differently.
S8: What to watch next: how much big tech plans to spend on AI next year, the Fed's decision in December, new rules on AI and data centres, and who becomes Nvidia's next CEO.
